title: [Chapitre] V. Algèbre des figures : notes manuscrites (14/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (inferred from pp. 20-22). A 'figure' F is a family of subsets of an ambient set, with |F| = ⋃F. For A ∈ F, A° = A minus the union of the elements of F strictly contained in A (the 'open cell'). The sets A° partition |F|; this partition is the equivalence relation R_F. Each A is the union of the A'° with A' ⊂ A, A' ∈ F. The frontier axiom used throughout is: B° ∩ B' ≠ ∅ ⇒ B ⊂ B'. In effect, a figure is an abstract stratified / cell-complex structure satisfying the frontier condition.

The proposition (p. 20) compares two figures F and G under two conditions.
- (a) For every A ∈ F, G^A = {B ∈ G : A ⊂ B} has a smallest element, and every A ∩ B (A ∈ F, B ∈ G) is F-closed in |F|, i.e. a union of elements of F.
- (b) For every A ∈ F there is a (necessarily unique) B = φ(A) ∈ G with A° ⊂ B°, and φ : F → G is increasing.

Page 21 finishes (b) ⇒ (a).
1. A ⊂ φ(A). Write A = ⋃_{A' ⊂ A} A'°. For each such A' let B' = φ(A'). Monotonicity gives B' ⊂ B, so A'° ⊂ B'° ⊂ B, hence A ⊂ B.
2. B is the least element of G^A. If B' ∈ G and A ⊂ B', then A° ⊂ B° ∩ B', so B° ∩ B' ≠ ∅. The frontier axiom in G gives B ⊂ B'.
3. A ∩ B is F-closed. Condition (b) means |F| ⊂ |G| and R_F is finer than the restriction of R_G to |F|. So A ∩ B is R_F-saturated: A is R_F-saturated and B is R_G-saturated. Hence A ∩ B = ⋃{C° : C ∈ F, C° ⊂ A ∩ B}.
4. One wants to replace each C° by C. C ⊂ A follows from the frontier axiom in F. C ⊂ B requires the implication (C ∈ F, B ∈ G, C° ⊂ B ⇒ C ⊂ B).
5. Grothendieck believes this needs a 'complément à l'énoncé'. He therefore states a Corollary: (b) ⇔ (b'), where (b') = [∀A ∃B with A° ⊂ B°] together with [A° ⊂ B ⇒ A ⊂ B]. A margin note adds (b''): R_F is finer than the R_G induced on |F|, plus a closure condition.
6. Page 22 proves (b') ⇒ monotonicity of φ. It then defines F ≪ G ('F est un raffinement de G') as the equivalent conditions, which is an order relation. It then starts a proposition characterising refinements that are minimal or have the same support: |F| = |G|.

Purpose: an axiomatic, purely set-theoretic 'algebra of figures', i.e. a combinatorial theory of cell decompositions and their subdivisions. This is plausibly in the spirit of the tame-topology programme of the Esquisse.
errors: Not a real gap: the implication C° ⊂ B ⇒ C ⊂ B already follows from (b), assuming cells are nonempty. Step 1 shows C ⊂ φ(C). Since C° ⊂ φ(C)° and C° ⊂ B, we get φ(C)° ∩ B ≠ ∅, so φ(C) ⊂ B by the frontier axiom in G, hence C ⊂ B. The 'complément' (b') is therefore redundant rather than necessary, though the corollary b ⇔ b' remains true.
Implicit assumption that every A° is nonempty, needed in steps 2 and 4. It is presumably part of the definition of a figure on earlier pages.
Minor slip: the page writes 'prouvons B ⊂ B' ou encore B° ∩ B' ≠ ∅'. It is the frontier axiom that makes these equivalent; only the direction B° ∩ B' ≠ ∅ ⇒ B ⊂ B' is used.

ideas.what: Refinement of figures: every open cell of F lies in an open cell of G, with the induced map on cells increasing. Equivalently, each cell of F has a smallest G-cell containing it and intersections of cells are F-closed.
ideas.modern_name: subdivision / refinement of a (regular) cell complex or stratification; poset map between face posets (carrier map)
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical PL topology and stratification theory (Whitehead, Zeeman; Whitney/Thom/Mather for stratifications)

ideas.what: Equivalence-relation formulation: R_F is finer than the R_G induced on |F|, so G-closed sets are R_F-saturated.
ideas.modern_name: a stratification refining another (partition refinement compatible with the frontier condition)

ideas.what: The least element φ(A) of G^A: the smallest G-cell containing a given F-cell.
ideas.modern_name: carrier of a cell in a subdivision

missed.claim: This page belongs to a 1986 axiomatic 'algebra of figures': a set-theoretic theory of cell decompositions with the frontier condition and their refinements. It is a concrete trace of Grothendieck working on foundations of combinatorial or tame geometry after the Esquisse. The page itself only contains routine lemmas.
missed.quote: Corollaire La condition b) équivaut à : b') ∀A∈F ∃B∈G tel que A°⊂B°, et d'autre part (A∈F, B∈G, A°⊂B implique A⊂B.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is of historical interest for reconstructing what Grothendieck meant by 'topologie modérée' and figures, and its relation to o-minimal cell decompositions. It offers no new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: These are elementary verifications about refinements of abstract cell decompositions, standard in PL and stratification theory. The only notable point is the redundant extra hypothesis Grothendieck thought he needed. Interest is purely archival and contextual.
